bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to "Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Commercial Water Heating Equipment".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the final rule titled Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Commercial Water Heating Equipment , which was submitted by the Department of Energy on October 6, 2023. The rule adopts more stringent energy conservation standards for commercial water heating equipment under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act in order to achieve more energy savings.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block a Department of Energy rule that set stricter energy efficiency standards for commercial water heaters. The rule, finalized in October 2023, was designed to reduce energy consumption by commercial water heating equipment. If passed, the resolution would nullify these updated standards and leave the previous, less stringent requirements in place.

industries.rationale: Manufacturers of commercial water heating equipment would face different regulatory compliance requirements depending on whether the energy efficiency standards are blocked or remain in effect.
Hotels and other hospitality businesses are major users of commercial water heating equipment and would be affected by changes in equipment efficiency standards and costs.
Restaurants and other retail establishments that rely on commercial water heating would face different equipment costs and energy expenses under the competing standards.
Hospitals and healthcare facilities use commercial water heating equipment and would be affected by changes in equipment efficiency requirements and operating costs.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the final rule titled Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Commercial Water Heating Equipment, which was submitted by the Energy Department on October 6, 2023.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who pays an energy bill.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in your energy bill. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
